name: Meal prep
lead: Meal prep is the practice of planning and cooking meals in advance, often a week at a time, and storing them in portioned containers [1]. In fitness and appearance communities it is used to hit calorie and protein targets consistently, which is how many people lose body fat or build muscle: a diet that is easy to follow is one that gets followed, and having cooked portions ready reduces unplanned or convenience eating.

Wikipedia notes people use it to lose weight, build muscle or keep a healthy lifestyle, and links frequent home cooking with lower type 2 diabetes risk [1]. A small published pilot study reported that a six-week group-based advanced meal prep course improved cooking attitudes, behaviours and body composition [2].

Meal prep is a habit rather than a product, and its relevance to looks runs through diet adherence: portion control, steady protein for training, and fewer decisions at mealtimes. It is also associated with saving money compared with eating out [1].

paras: Fully cooked meals are made ahead to standardise portions and are often stored in small labelled, dated containers [1]. Related services include meal kits and meal delivery companies.

The pilot program in the research literature had participants meet weekly in a commercial kitchen to prepare meals in bulk and package individual portions, taking home 10 meals and 5 snacks each week [2]. Meal prep sits alongside meal kits and delivery services as ways to shift cooking time and decisions earlier in the week.

Bodybuilding-style diets rely on repeatable meals: the same protein, carbohydrate and vegetable portions at set times. Users prepare them in batches so that fixed targets are hit without daily cooking. On looksmax.org, a member describing a diet of fasting and low-carbohydrate eating complained that broccoli and chicken breast were boring and asked for low-carb prep ideas [4], and another thread asked whether UK members used meal prep companies [3].

Wikipedia cites a restaurant menu markup of around 300 percent and US figures showing food-at-home spending rising 6.4 percent while food-away-from-home spending fell 32.6 percent between 2019 and 2020, estimating that the average consumer saved about $1,151 by eating out less [1].

Cohort analyses cited by Wikipedia link eating home-prepared meals more often with a lower risk of type 2 diabetes, and associate more ultra-processed food and eating out with higher risk of hypertension, dyslipidaemia or cancer; a systematic review found frequent eating out associated with higher sugar and fat intake and lower iron, calcium and vitamin C intake [1]. These studies concern home cooking in general rather than batch preparation specifically.

Pre-cooked food can grow bacteria if stored improperly or eaten too late, and plastic containers can shed microplastics, particularly when microwaved [1]. Wikipedia also notes that over-structured prepping can lead to rigidity or a food rut [1].
Wikipedia also notes that freezing can make plastic containers more brittle and that "microwave-safe" labelling describes structural integrity more than chemical safety [1].
Meal prep is discussed alongside bodybuilding-style diets and low-carbohydrate eating, with users asking about prep ideas and meal prep companies in forum threads [3][4].
Discussion tends to be practical: what to cook, which services to use, and how to make restricted diets tolerable. Meal prep is rarely the subject of claims; it is treated as logistics for a diet.

A pilot study in Current Developments in Nutrition tested a group-based advance quantity meal prep (AQMP) program in participants recruited from a fitness center, with one group measured before the program, right after it and three months later. The program met weekly for six weeks in a commercial kitchen. Cooking attitude scores rose from baseline to three months, cooking self-efficacy rose by the end of the program, and reported home-cooked dinners increased from about 52 percent to 86 percent. Mean body weight fell from 85.1 kg to 83.3 kg at three months, fat mass fell from 32.0 kg to 28.6 kg, and BMI fell from 31.7 to 31.0 at the end of the program. The authors describe it as a pilot and call for larger controlled studies [2][6].

A pilot of a community meal-kit service in Washington DC studied vegetable intake and barriers to healthy eating rather than appearance [5]. No trial has compared meal prep with other adherence strategies for body composition.

claims.claim: Cooking in bulk makes it easier to stick to a low-carb or high-protein diet
claims.believers: Members asking for low-carb meal prep ideas describe bland repeated meals such as chicken and broccoli and look for variety to keep the diet going [4].
claims.experts: A six-week pilot reported higher home-cooked dinner consumption and lower body weight and fat mass at follow-up in participants of a meal prep course, without a control group [2][6].

claims.claim: Using a meal prep company is a convenient alternative to cooking
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread asked whether UK members use meal prep companies [3].
claims.experts: A pilot meal-kit study in Washington DC examined dietary disparities and vegetable intake rather than appearance outcomes [5].

card.summary: Cook ahead, portion it out; a habit tool for hitting diet targets, with small studies linking it to better habits.
card.note: Food-safety storage matters for pre-cooked meals.

quick.overview:
Meal prep means cooking and portioning meals in advance, usually weekly. Fitness communities use it to keep calories and protein on target.

Studies are small. One six-week program reported better cooking habits and body composition.
quick.mechanism: Having portioned meals ready reduces decision-making and unplanned eating, which supporters say makes a diet easier to follow.
quick.risks: Stored cooked food can grow bacteria if kept or reheated improperly, and some plastic containers can shed microplastics when heated.

chain: Meals planned, cooked and portioned in advance
Calories and protein are set before hunger hits
Easier adherence to a cut or bulk, leading to a leaner or more muscular physique
angle.text: People batch-cook and portion meals so their calories and protein are decided ahead of time. In a cutting or bulking phase this makes the plan easier to follow day to day, which is the route to the physique result.
